Consult Summary:
- Acute eczema flare with intense itch and dry, cracked red skin affecting the chest, hands, and inner elbows; plan includes a stronger topical corticosteroid, emollients, and antihistamines with follow-up in 7–10 days.

History:
- Presenting complaint
  - Several days of very itchy, red, and sore skin; described as “super annoying” and disruptive to sleep and work.
  - Areas affected: chest, hands, and inner elbows; no facial involvement reported.
- Onset and timeline
  - Symptoms started approximately four days ago.
  - Patient had tried a steroid cream purchased from a pharmacy last night without improvement.
  - Previously diagnosed with eczema; had used prescribed eczema creams in the past.
- Exacerbating, initiating, or relieving factors
  - No clear trigger identified; patient considered changing products (e.g., shower gel or clothing) but has not confirmed a specific cause.
  - No fever or systemic symptoms.
- Associated symptoms / systems review
  - No respiratory symptoms; no chest breathing issues; bowels and urination reportedly normal.
  - No bleeding or discharge from the skin; some cracking of the skin noted.
- Past medical history
  - History of eczema.
  - Asthma in the past, but not currently active.
- Medications
  - No regular medications reported.
  - Recently used an over-the-counter steroid cream with limited effect.
- Allergies
  - Denies allergies.
- Social history
  - Age 31; lives with a few flatmates; full-time job at a pharmaceutical company.
  - Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol use: occasional beer a few times per week.
- Family history
  - Not discussed.
